source.author: verg
source.text: Hinc Italae gentes omnisque Oenotria tellus in dubiis responsa petunt; huc dona sacerdos Cum tulit et caesarum ovium sub nocte silenti pellibus incubuit stratis somnosque petivit, multa modis simulacra videt volitantia miris et varias audit voces fruiturque deorum couloquio atque imis Acheronta affatur Avernis.
source.text_original: Hinc Italae gentes omnisque Oenotria tellus / in dubiis responsa petunt; huc dona sacerdos / Cum tulit et caesarum ovium sub nocte silenti / pellibus incubuit stratis somnosque petivit, / multa modis simulacra videt volitantia miris / et varias audit voces fruiturque deorum / couloquio atque imis Acheronta affatur Avernis.
source.text_english: From here the peoples of Italy and all the land of Oenotria seek answers in times of doubt; here the priest brings gifts, and when under the silent night he has lain down on the spread skins of the slaughtered sheep, he seeks sleep, and sees many apparitions flitting in wondrous forms, hears various voices, and enjoys converse with the gods, and speaks with Acheron deep in Avernus.

reuse.author: val
reuse.text: mitte metus, volat ille mari quantumque propinquat, iam magis atque magis variis stupet Aea deorum prodigiis quatiuntque truces oracula Colchos.
reuse.text_original: 'mitte metus, volat ille mari quantumque propinquat, / iam magis atque magis variis stupet Aea deorum / prodigiis quatiuntque truces oracula Colchos.
reuse.text_english: Dismiss your fears; he is flying over the sea, and the nearer he draws, the more and more Aea is amazed at the various portents of the gods, and the fierce oracles shake the Colchians.
